conflict_topics: immediate access to seat vs. current occupant's use
dialogue_quality_notes: Agent C repeats the same reassurance multiple times ('I'll tell you when it's free; shouldn't be long.'), producing some redundancy.
Agent B consistently asserts a property-rights stance ('I already sat here... my bowl's open so I can't move it.') and does not engage further after initial refusal.
Agent D's corroboration of the tissue packet is factual evidence but does not by itself force a change in others' positions.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A abandoned the immediate demand and agreed to wait while Agent C finishes; Agent C committed to notify A when the seat is free. Key lines: Turn 9 Agent C: 'I'm almost done — won't be long.' Turn 10 Agent A: 'Okay, Agent C — I'll step off the aisle. Tell me when the seat's free; my food's hot.' Turn 11 Agent C: 'Okay, I'll tell you when it's free.'
position_change_notes: Agent A changed position: from requesting immediate seating and asking B to move (Rounds 1–4) to accepting to step off the aisle and wait for the seat (Round 5). Evidence: Turn 10.
Agent C committed to notify A when the seat is free and repeatedly reassured A (Rounds 5–8). Evidence: Turns 9, 11, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30.
Agent B retained their original position of keeping the seat and did not make concessions; B reiterated refusal in Round 4 (Turn 7) and was silent thereafter.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 Agent A claims the tissue as a reservation and asks to sit; Turn 2 Agent B refuses, saying 'I already sat here... my bowl's open so I can't move it.' Direct, opposing claims over the seat.

Turn 3 Agent A repeats the request to move the bowl; Turn 4 Agent C proposes a compromise ('Agent A, can you step a little off the aisle? Agent B, could you nudge your bowl a bit if that's possible?'), introducing a possible accommodation though no agreement yet from B.

Turn 5 Agent D corroborates A ('I saw Agent A leave that tissue packet here earlier'), and Turn 6 Agent A repeats the demand citing that witness. The corroboration raises the stakes for B's continued refusal (B has not yielded).
Turn 7 Agent B reiterates refusal and restates boundary ('...please wait until I'm finished or find another spot.'), and Turn 8 Agent A asks how long. Positions remain opposed with no new agreement.

Turn 9 Agent C signals they are 'almost done — won't be long.' Turn 10 Agent A accepts waiting and agrees to step off the aisle ('Okay, Agent C — I'll step off the aisle. Tell me when the seat's free; my food's hot.'). A's acceptance to wait and C's promise to inform constitute a mutual spoken arrangement resolving the immediate conflict over sitting now.
Turn 11 and Turn 14 Agent C repeats the commitment ('Okay, I'll tell you when it's free; shouldn't be long.'). No opposing demands reappear.
Turn 18 and Turn 22 Agent C continues to reassure they will notify when the seat is free. No substantive disagreement is expressed.
Turn 26 and Turn 30 Agent C repeats the same assurance ('I'll tell you when it's free. Shouldn't be long.'). The earlier arrangement stands and no further contestation occurs.

substantive_insights: A claimed a low-effort reservation (tissue packet) and used a corroborating witness (D) to reinforce the claim, which increased leverage but did not override the occupant's immediate use.
The conflict was resolved when the claimant (A) accepted a wait rather than immediate access; C played a facilitative role by promising to notify when the seat freed up.
B never agreed to move, so the practical state (B occupying a seat) remained uncontested; resolution depended on A's concession to wait rather than B conceding the seat.
